# Catalog

## Durations
- `instant` 0.1s
- `responsive` 0.2s
- `expressive` 0.35s
- `exit` 0.26s
- `slow` 0.6s
- `linger` 1.4s
- `snap` 0.3s
- `drift` 1s

## Eases
- `linear` — linear
- `out` — cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94)
- `inOut` — cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)
- `responsive` — spring, visual 0.2s, bounce 0
- `expressive` — spring, visual 0.35s, bounce 0.12
- `steep` — cubic-bezier(0.87, 0, 0.13, 1)
- `pop` — spring, visual 0.3s, bounce 0.3
- `whip` — whip

## Staggers
- `char` 20ms
- `word` 40ms
- `line` 80ms
- `list` 40ms
- `grid` 40ms

## Enter presets
| Preset | Animates | Duration | Ease | Mask | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fade` | opacity | settles ≈ 0.35s | responsive |  | Opacity only. Quiet: secondary copy, a surface appearing in place. |
| `rise` | y, opacity | settles ≈ 0.35s | responsive |  | Fade up by litt's travel (32px). The workhorse for copy, rows and cards. |
| `slideLeft` | x, opacity | settles ≈ 0.35s | responsive |  | Slide in from the right by travel, moving left (reading direction). |
| `slideRight` | x, opacity | settles ≈ 0.35s | responsive |  | Slide in from the left by travel, moving right. |
| `settle` | y, scale, opacity | settles ≈ 0.58s | expressive |  | Placed, not thrown: rises by travel and settles from 0.98 on the expressive spring. The scene's one moment (a statement, the product). |
| `maskUp` | yPct | settles ≈ 0.35s | responsive | yes | Lines or words rise from behind their baseline. Use with split; pass ease "expressive" when it is the scene's moment. |
| `grow` | scaleY | settles ≈ 0.35s | responsive |  | Grow from the baseline (scaleY; bars, rails). Set transform-origin at the base — BarChart does. |
| `wipeRight` | clipRight | slow (0.6s) | inOut |  | Clip reveal left → right, for data: a chart behind its playhead, a timeline strip. |
| `draw` | draw | slow (0.6s) | inOut |  | A stroke draws on (Path, LineChart's line). Data only. |
| `typeOn` | opacity | 0.001s | linear |  | Characters appear one by one (split: 'chars', or m.type). UI and terminal typing. |
| `whip` | x, opacity, blurX | settles ≈ 1s | whip |  | Energetic register. Whip and drift: 85% of the way in ~1.5 frames (motion-blurred), then a slow drift for the rest of the `drift` (1s). dir: left (default), right, up, down; distance default 160. Land it on a beat. |

## Exit presets
| Preset | Animates | Duration | Ease | Mask | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fadeOut` | opacity | 0.75× the entrance (≤ 0.26s) | out |  | Opacity to zero, at 0.75× the entrance. |
| `liftOut` | y, opacity | 0.75× the entrance (≤ 0.26s) | out |  | Lift by half the travel and fade: clears the stage for what comes next. |
| `dropOut` | y, opacity | 0.75× the entrance (≤ 0.26s) | out |  | Sink back by half the travel and fade (the reverse of rise). |
| `maskOut` | yPct | 0.75× the entrance (≤ 0.26s) | out | yes | Lines or words leave upward behind the mask. |
| `scaleOut` | scale, opacity | 0.75× the entrance (≤ 0.26s) | out |  | Back to 0.98 and fade (the reverse of settle). |

## Emphasis presets
| Preset | Animates | Duration | Ease | Mask | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ink` | ink | instant (0.1s) | out |  | Step up to fg from the grey, at the instant tier. litt ranks by ink: the word that matters brightens. |
| `dim` | ink | instant (0.1s) | out |  | Step back to the grey from fg, at the instant tier, so something else leads. |
| `press` | scale | instant (0.1s) | out |  | A button press: scale to 0.98 at the instant tier, back on the responsive spring. |

## Scene transitions (storyboard `transition`)
| type | default | range | params | what it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cut` | — | — | — | Hard cut, on the beat. The primary: most of a litt edit is cuts. |
| `match` | 0.6s | 0.3–1.2s | ease, pairs | A match cut: a hard cut where each paired element of the incoming scene starts exactly where its partner was in the outgoing one (place and size, measured), then settles into its own place over the duration, so the eye carries straight across the cut. If the partner is moving at the cut (≥ 60 px/s), the element leaves the cut at that velocity and slows into its place on one curve (place it ⅓–⅔ of speed × duration along the travel, or it must speed up after the cut); its fill (only between two opaque solid fills) and corner radius start as the partner's and turn into its own. pairs: ["logo"] (same id) or [["ring", "badge"]]. A primary move, like a cut: it is not an accent. |
| `carry` | 0.5s | 0.3–1s | dir, distance, blur, layers | A cut on movement: the camera is already travelling when the cut lands. The outgoing scene accelerates in the direction of travel (dir, default left), the cut swaps the scenes at peak speed, and the incoming one decelerates from that same speed to rest — two shots, one move. distance: % of the frame (default 8, a drift; 30–60 in the energetic register is a whip pan); blur follows the speed. Each scene only translates (no zoom), so every point of the frame keeps one speed through the cut; while it travels its backdrop bleeds past the edge, so no edge shows. A primary move, like a cut. |
| `crossfade` | 0.4s | 0.25–0.8s | ease | The incoming scene fades over the outgoing one. The same surface in a new state. |
| `dip` | 0.5s | 0.3–1s | ease | Out fades to the canvas, then in fades up. A breath between chapters, before the end card. |
| `push` | 0.5s | 0.3–0.8s | ease, dir, blur, layers | The incoming scene pushes the outgoing one off in the direction of travel (dir, default left = reading order). Sequential steps. blur: true when it moves fast. |
| `pushUp` | 0.5s | 0.3–0.8s | ease, blur, layers | push with dir up: the incoming scene pushes up from below. Lists, feeds, 9:16. |
| `wipe` | 0.5s | 0.35–0.8s | ease, dir, angle, feather | The incoming scene wipes on with a moving edge (dir, default right). feather (8–20) softens it; angle (e.g. 120) runs it diagonally. A state revealed. |
| `pixels` | 0.5s | 0.3–0.8s | ease, dir | Energetic register. A digital cut through the canvas: square cells (a 24th of the frame's long side) of the canvas colour dissolve over the outgoing scene in an ordered dither, then the incoming scene appears through the same dither, both sweeping in the direction of travel (dir, default right). No frame mixes two scenes' type. The product loads, a machine takes over. |
| `depth` | 0.6s | 0.4–1s | ease, dir (dir: in/out) | Energetic register. The camera flies through the stack: the outgoing scene grows past the viewer as the next one comes forward from behind (dir in, default). dir out is the reverse — close a reel by flying back out of where it opened. |
| `morph` | 0.6s | 0.3–1.2s | ease, pairs, squash, arc | A shared element carries the cut: each pair travels from its place in the outgoing scene to its place in the incoming one (position and size; shapes morph their outline) while the rest crossfades under it — the scenes flow instead of cutting. pairs: ["logo"] (same id) or [["title", "card"]]; squash 0..0.5 for mass; arc bends the path. |
| `portal` | 0.8s | 0.5–1.4s | ease, dir, via (dir: in/out) | The camera goes through an element. dir in (default): the outgoing scene grows until via (one of its elements: a card, a screen, a button) fills the frame, and the incoming scene is what was inside it, opening from the element's rounded rect. dir out: the outgoing scene shrinks into via, an element of the incoming scene (a pull-back to the screen it was playing on). The two scenes move as one rig, measured, so the window stays locked to the element. |

One transition language per video: cuts on the beat, and at most two accent types (three once a scene is energetic) — see motion-craft §8.

## Registers (storyboard / scene `register`, docs/decisions/0007)
The look is litt in every register; the register sets the motion's energy and the lint bounds below.

| register | bounce ≤ | moments/scene | travel ≤ | ambient zoom ≤ | camera ≤ | movers ≤ | accents ≤ | loops | copy types or wipes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `calm` | 0.12 | 1 | 64px | 3% | 15%/s · 160px/s | 5 | 2 | warning | — |
| `energetic` | 0.35 | 3 | 160px | 8% | 50%/s · 480px/s | 7 | 3 | info | yes (text-fade) |

- `calm` — litt as written: responsive springs, one expressive moment per scene, cuts on the beat, the camera's slow push.
- `energetic` — A brand reel or montage: steep in-outs for UI and camera, pop springs for objects, linear for machines, depth moves, bursts then holds.

## Type scale (`text-<step>`: px · line height px · tracking, at 1080 short side; 9:16 in brackets)
- `text-display` 112 · 112 · -0.04em
- `text-title` 48 · 56 · -0.025em (9:16: 56 · 64)
- `text-body` 36 · 48 · -0.01em (9:16: 40 · 52)
- `text-small` 30 · 40 · -0.005em (9:16: 36 · 48)
- `text-label` 28 · 36 · 0em (9:16: 34 · 44)

Weights by role: `font-normal` 400 text · `font-title` 500 titles · `font-label` 600 labels (the label step only).

## Themes
- `litt-dark` (dark) — litt, dark: a warm near-black canvas, stepped stone surfaces, one cobalt accent that behaves like light.
- `litt-light` (light) — litt, light: a warm off-white canvas, white raised surfaces, the same cobalt accent as a cool light.

## Type kit
- `litt` — Geist in three weights by role, Geist Mono for code and data. One display step per scene; rank from weight, two inks and space. Display Geist 500 · text Geist 400 · mono Geist Mono 400 · figures: sans.

## Timeline lint rules
- `ease-linear` — Spatial motion with a linear ease looks mechanical. Use a token ease (the responsive or expressive spring, out, inOut, steep). Energetic register: linear rotation is fine for a machine (a spinning ring).
- `duration-too-fast` — Spatial entrances/exits under 150ms read as glitches.
- `duration-too-slow` — Entrances/exits/emphasis over 1.6s drag. Split it, or make it a camera move.
- `duration-off-token` — Durations should come from the token scale (instant/responsive/expressive/exit/slow/linger, snap in the energetic register) for a consistent rhythm.
- `exit-slower-than-enter` — Exits should be quicker than entrances (attention has moved on).
- `settle-interrupted` — A new tween on the same property starts before the previous one settled — motion never lands.
- `read-time` — Text must stay long enough to read — ≈17 chars/s + 0.4s (min 0.83s) counted from when it starts appearing — and hold ≥ 0.6s once fully landed.
- `retype-hold` — A retyped phrase (m.retype) must be readable before its first key is deleted: ≈17 chars/s + 0.4s from when it starts typing, and ≥ 0.6s complete.
- `cycle-glance` — A word in a Cycle (m.cycle) is on show for under 0.25s between flips: it reads as flicker, not as a list. Fewer words, or more time between steps.
- `hold-too-short` — Element exits almost as soon as it lands.
- `ui-glance` — UI mockup text should be fully landed for ≥ 0.8s so it registers (it is imagery, not copy — no full read time needed).
- `scene-overrun` — Motion is still running after the scene has ended (it will be cut off).
- `late-entrance` — Element enters in the last moments of the scene — it pops in and is gone.
- `dead-air` — Nothing moves for too long (2.5s; energetic register: 1.6s, a hold is about a second). Let the camera carry the hold (a push of 3% or less) or tighten the scene.
- `crowded` — Too many independent elements animating at once — the eye can't follow (calm: 5, energetic: 7).
- `unstaggered-group` — Several elements enter with the same preset at the same instant. Stagger them to create hierarchy.
- `slow-open` — The video's first motion starts late — the opening frame is dead.
- `split-too-busy` — Character split on long copy is slow and noisy. Split by words or lines instead.
- `stagger-too-long` — The stagger cascade takes too long to complete.
- `camera-too-fast` — Camera moves faster than ~15% zoom/s or 160px/s feel jarring (energetic register: 50% zoom/s, 480px/s). A pan is x and y with their shifts.
- `dead-cut` — A plain cut between two rests: the outgoing scene has settled and the incoming one starts still, so the eye stops at the join. Cut on movement (an exit into the cut, an entrance on it, or a carry), match it, or go through an element (portal, morph).
- `static-edit` — Most of the film's joins carry nothing (dead cuts, crossfades, dips): it reads as a slideshow. Let the joins flow — carry, match, portal, morph, push — and keep the still cuts as punctuation.
- `transition-too-long` — A transition longer than its type's craft range stalls the edit (a 1s push is no longer a step).
- `transition-too-short` — A transition shorter than its type's range reads as a glitch, not a move.
- `transition-language` — More than two accent transition types in one video reads as a template (three once any scene is energetic). Pick one primary (most cuts) and few accents; hard cuts are free.
- `transition-register` — This transition belongs to another register (e.g. depth is energetic). Set the scene's register, or pick a transition from its own.
- `transition-bounce` — Spring overshoot on a full-frame scene move looks cheap. Use a bezier ease (inOut, out).
- `transition-strobe` — A fast push without motion blur jumps over 200px a frame and strobes. Add blur: true, or lengthen it.
- `mask-needs-split` — Mask presets reveal from behind a clip edge — use split (words/lines) or wrap the element in an overflow-hidden parent.
- `cut-off-beat` — Scene cut is not on the beat. With music, time the scene in beats (duration: { beats: 8 }) so its cut lands on one; without it, the bare bpm grid is checked (info).
- `off-beat` — A move starts one to three frames off a beat or hit: it reads as late, not as syncopated. Snap it (snap: "beat") or move it decisively off the grid.
- `axis-reflow` — Weight/width animation changes letter widths: wrapping text re-breaks its lines mid-motion. Split chars/words, or keep the line nowrap.
- `axis-unsupported` — The element's family has no such axis, so the channel animates nothing (e.g. wdth or soft on Geist, which has a weight axis only).
- `axis-range` — Axis values outside what the family can draw are clamped: the motion flatlines at the end of its range.
- `spring-bounce` — litt: a spring bounces at 0.12 or less (the expressive tier). More reads as a toy. Energetic register: up to 0.35, for things that act like objects (the pop spring).
- `exit-bounce` — litt: exits never bounce. They ease out at 0.75× the entrance (the exit presets do it).
- `expressive-budget` — litt: one expressive moment per scene (the statement, or the product placed). Every other entrance is responsive. Energetic register: up to three (a group counts once).
- `material-motion` — litt P5: material is static. Tween the backdrop never; a gradient field moves by itself. The light, glow and grain never animate, loop or sweep.
- `property-motion` — litt: transform and opacity animate, plus ink at the instant tier, masks and data (draw, counter, a cell's radius). Tracking, weight, blur and filters perform.
- `travel-too-far` — litt: entrances travel 32px (litt's 16 at video scale). Further reads as thrown, not placed. Energetic register: collage pieces may land from up to 160px. The distance is x and y with their shifts (shiftX, shiftY).
- `camera-edge` — The camera shows past the edge of the scene: a pan can be at most what the zoom adds (|x| ≤ (scale − 1) × half the width, the same for y), and the camera never zooms below 1.
- `camera-drift` — The ambient camera push stays within 3% over its scene: it is the only ambient life, and it must not be noticed (energetic register: 8%).
- `ambient-loop` — litt: motion that is not a response never performs. No loops (floating cards, breathing glows); the camera's slow push is the ambient life. A caret blink is fine (m.blink). Energetic register: an info — an object may spin or swing (a ring, a keychain), never copy.
- `text-fade` — Energetic register: copy never just fades in. It types on (m.type) or wipes on like a selection (wipeRight, or the selection-block recipe).
- `weight-role` — litt P9: three weights by role — 400 text, 500 titles, 600 labels. A weight tween settles on one of them.
- `ease-register` — Whip and drift and squash-and-stretch perform: they belong to the energetic register (a reel, a beat-cut film). A calm scene places things with springs.

## Source lint rules
- `nondeterministic-api` — Wall-clock / random APIs (Math.random, Date.now, new Date(), performance.now, setTimeout/setInterval, requestAnimationFrame) in project code — frames are seeked, so results must be a pure function of time. Use the motion DSL; for variety use fixed data or a seeded sequence.
- `css-animation` — CSS animation/transition (style `animation:`/`transition:` or Tailwind `animate-*`/`transition*` classes) — real-time CSS motion is invisible to seeking and drifts between workers. Animate with `motion: (m) => …` instead.
- `litt-weight` — A weight outside litt's three roles (P9) — text is 400 (font-normal, the default), titles 500 (font-title, Headline and Title), labels 600 (font-label, Label). No medium, semibold, bold or light.
- `litt-case` — Uppercase text — litt sets every label in sentence case. Use Label (600, the grey), never an uppercase eyebrow.
- `litt-gradient` — A hand-made gradient (gradient text, a fill, a border, a faint glow behind the content) — a backdrop is one colour or a moving field (Stage bg="gradient"). Everything else is a flat token colour.
- `litt-radius` — A radius off litt's scale — rounded-control (8) for controls and tags, rounded-surface (16) for cards and panels, rounded-full for avatars, icon buttons and switches. Nothing else.
- `litt-shadow` — An ad-hoc or offset shadow (P4) — use the depth tokens: shadow-raised (cards), shadow-float / shadow-modal / shadow-tooltip (floating), shadow-glow (the one primary action), shadow-hairline / shadow-control / shadow-field / shadow-lift / shadow-focus.
- `litt-accent-text` — Accent-coloured text — litt never picks out a headline word in the accent. Rank by ink: the key word in text-fg, the rest in text-fg-muted (or m.emphasize(id, "ink")).
- `litt-hex` — A hard-coded colour — every colour is a litt token (bg-canvas, text-fg-muted, border-line, data hues…), so both themes stay designed.
- `svg-overflow` — An inline <svg> with overflow visible — under a transform that changes every frame (a camera push) Chrome rasterises its edges by what the worker drew before, so frames differ between renders. Keep the svg clipped to its viewBox (widen the viewBox instead), or use <Shape>.
